enumeration_note: The video teaches one VWAP-band-breakout skeleton, first in a raw 2:1 form, then refined with EMA-trend and POC-in-bands confirmation filters at a 1.5:1 target. These share the same breakout entry and swing-based stop, differing only by added confirmation mechanics and target-R â€” enumerated as one strategy with two variants.

coaching_notes: Traders usually try to avoid consolidating markets, by using the V-wap bands we can do exactly that.

Even though the V-wap indicator is very useful and powerful we can still see that there are a lot of false signals that are still being provided with this strategy. To filter out these false trades... let's add two more indicators to the chart.
element_inventory: Long entry: price breaks out above the upper VWAP band
Short entry: price breaks below the lower VWAP band
Long stop: recent swing low (place slightly below the VWAP line if the swing is near VWAP)
Short stop: recent swing high (place just above the VWAP line if nearby)
Trend filter (filtered variant): CM EMA Trend Bars with EMA up-trend set to 200 â€” green bar required for longs, red bar for shorts
POC precondition (filtered variant): volume-profile Point of Control must be within the VWAP bands at the moment of breakout
Volume Profile Fixed Range config: row size 36, number of bars 300
strategies.entry_summary: Trade a breakout of the VWAP bands: enter long when price breaks above the upper VWAP band, enter short when price breaks below the lower VWAP band. A filtered variant additionally requires trend confirmation (CM EMA Trend Bars, 200 EMA â€” green candles for longs, red for shorts) and that the volume-profile Point of Control sits within the VWAP bands at the moment of the breakout.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop at the recent swing low (longs) / recent swing high (shorts) â€” placed slightly beyond the VWAP line if the swing is close to it. Take profit at a fixed R-multiple: 2:1 in the base band-breakout variant, 1.5:1 in the filtered variant.
